blocks.text: Read the chapter with this setting in view: Isaiah names Cyrus as YHWH's shepherd and anointed agent for Babylon's defeat and Jerusalem's restoration without depicting Cyrus as an Israelite Davidic king. It gives a starting point for following the chapter's own movement. The chapter itself should determine how far the point is taken. A more precise reconstruction remains disputed.

A literary feature to notice is that Isaiah 40-55 announces comfort and return from Babylon through creation and exodus imagery, presenting a new homecoming without implying that displacement trauma or postreturn conflict simply vanished. This form helps organize the chapter's claims. Notice it before drawing broader conclusions from a single phrase or image. Interpretations differ on some details.
